subject: Request: temporary burst window increase for HelixCare launch
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@helixcare.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <ops@helixcare.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch spike / temporary burst increase request

Hi Evelyn —

Quick note from the HelixCare launch team. We’re ramping up a national rollout of a new appointment booking flow on April 20 and our traffic projections (attached) show sustained traffic that will exceed our current Redwood burst window and fairness threshold. Summary:
- Baseline: 300 rps normal traffic per region.
- Current allowed burst config in our plan: 1,000 rps for up to 60s before throttling fairness kicks in.
- Expected: several sustained minutes at ~2,500 rps with short spikes up to 5,000 rps during promo pushes.

We need a temporary SLA-exception that gives HelixCare a higher burst window and a temporary relaxation of fairness throttling for 72 hours around the launch (target window: 2027-04-20T00:00Z to 2027-04-23T00:00Z). We’re happy to accept elevated costs for this window and any required pre-warm steps you recommend.

I attached a traffic projection CSV and a short impact analysis. Can Redwood confirm feasibility and provide:
1) whether you can lift the burst cap and for how long,
2) any SRE conditions (warm-up, cache priming),
3) estimated overage cost and how it will be invoiced, and
4) any risks to SLA (latency/availability) during the window.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround so we can finalize our go/no-go on Monday.

—Asha
Asha Rao
Director, Product Operations
HelixCare
[Attachment: helixcare_traffic_projection_q2.csv (text/csv)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@helixcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch spike / temporary burst increase request

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the projection and early heads-up. We can support temporary policy exceptions for launches like this, but we’ll need to do a quick review with SRE for an operational plan and a short addendum for the billing/exception term.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik (SE) to confirm technical approach and fallback options by EOD tomorrow.
- I’ll route an exception doc (SLA addendum) for legal review; once signed we can schedule a warm-up window.
- Please confirm the exact 72-hour window and whether HelixCare will accept priority routing and pre-warm fees.

If HelixCare can provide a minute-level timestamp sample (CSV is helpful) we can simulate load against the targeted model(s).

I’ve attached a short proposed SLA exemption template for your review.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_sla_exemption_term.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@helixcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch spike / temporary burst increase request

Hi team —

Quick technical readout after reviewing the projection:
- Current tenant limits for HelixCare (hosted plan): steady-state 300 rps, burst window configured up to 1,000 rps for 60s. Fairness policy will start soft-throttling when cluster-level saturation is detected (we cap tenants to ~65% of available capacity under contention).

Feasible options:
1) Temporary policy override (recommended for speed): raise burst cap to 4,000 rps with a 5-minute burst window and mark HelixCare as priority routing for 72 hours. Requires SRE sign-off and a signed addendum. Fallback: we will automatically downgrade requests to a lighter model if token consumption threatens overall latency.
2) Short-term Dedicated slot: reserve a small Dedicated pool for the window — more predictable and isolates fairness effects but requires capacity lead time (72 hours to provision) and a reserved commit.
3) Hybrid: Dedicated for peak minutes + policy override for remainder.

Operational requirements for option 1:
- Traffic pattern CSV (timestamped) for simulation.
- Pre-warm run 24 hours before launch (we’ll run synthetic traffic to populate KV caches).
- Explicit acceptance of elevated overage billing (we estimate $X/day for the override; final number after simulation).
- Monitoring playbook: HelixCare must assign an on-call contact during the window.

Risks: slight latency variance during very large spikes; if other customers concurrently have incidents, short-term throttling may still occur at the network ingress layer.

I can run the sim on Monday if you share minute-level logs.

—Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@helixcare.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch spike / temporary burst increase request

Evelyn / team —

SRE review summary and conditional approval: we can grant a temporary policy override for the dates proposed (2027-04-20T00:00Z -> 2027-04-23T00:00Z) under the following conditions:
1) HelixCare provides minute-level traffic for the last 14 days and final projected waveform at least 72 hours before start.
2) HelixCare agrees to priority routing and the pre-warm timeline: 24h warm-up window beginning 2027-04-19T00:00Z.
3) Redwood will enable a 5-minute burst window at up to 4,000 rps (configurable downward if sims fail).
4) If observed token-level consumption threatens cluster-wide SLOs, automatic model downgrade + soft-throttle will be applied — we will notify HelixCare within 1 minute of any throttling event.
5) Billing: overage will be invoiced as a one-off exception line item. Finance to provide estimate; legal to sign addendum.

We’ll need HelixCare to confirm acceptance of those conditions by EOD Monday. If accepted, I authorize scheduling the pre-warm and the simulation run.

Operational note: we’ll route traffic through our priority queue, which changes fairness weighting; this is reversible but not instantaneous — expect a 30–60 minute cooldown.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Production Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@helixcare.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch spike / temporary burst increase request

Thanks all — HelixCare team confirms and accepts the terms and timeline.

We will:
- Share 14 days of minute-level traffic by Monday 2027-04-12 23:59 UTC.
- Accept priority routing and pre-warm plan (2027-04-19T00:00Z warm-up).
- Sign the addendum and accept provisional overage invoicing for the 72-hour window.
- Assign on-call: raj.patel@helixcare.com for launch ops.

Please send the SLA addendum and final cost estimate and we’ll return a signed copy within 24 hours.

—Asha
Director, Product Operations
HelixCare
[Attachment: signed_intent_stub.pdf (application/pdf)]
